messages:
Ashley: quick follow-up to the layered profiles RFC — proposing a hot-swap playbook and concrete runtime contracts. main goals: per-op precision swaps without recompiles, deterministic fallback ordering, and tight canary instrumentation.

Devon: +1. big question: how do we identify ops across transforms/kernels? need a stable keying scheme and versioned op signatures so graph rewrites don't break overrides.

Leo: suggest canonical op-id: <model>::<module_path>::<op_kind>::<ordinal>. e.g. gpt2::blocks.3::attn_matmul::0. keeps it human-readable and stable across transforms.

Mia: for QA, we should attach a profile diff artifact to every rollout: per-profile deltas for exact-match/ROUGE/perp and token-level confidence heatmaps. also capture small "worst-10" prompt set for manual triage.

Ashley: runtime fallback priority proposal: user_hint > op_override > model_base. runtime computes a per-op stability score from telemetry (EMA of token_confidence and delta_perplexity). below threshold -> swap to higher precision for that op only.

Devon: implementation note: no on-the-fly kernel compiles. plan: pre-bake kernel variants into the instance pool images and expose a kernel table. hot-swap becomes pointer switch + cache rebind. if needed variant missing -> fall back to model_base_prec.

InfraBot: infra note: feature-flag available as "quant.hot_swap_canary". CI step "quant-canary-run" will run 3 workloads if flag enabled. images can be built with up to 3 kernel variants pre-baked.

SRE-Bot: alerting rules for canary: fire if 99p latency > +20% OR error-rate > 0.5% OR model-perp delta > +10%. create a temporary alert channel for canary windows.

Leo: schema extras: add fields for rounding_mode, quant_seed, fp8_format (e4m3|e5m2), calibration_alg. also include schema_version and compatibility field for older runtimes.

Ashley: example profile (sketch):
```json
{
  "profile_id": "layered-hot-swap-v1",
  "schema_version": "1",
  "model_base_precision": "int8",
  "op_overrides": {
    "gpt2::blocks.*::attn_matmul::*": { "precision": "fp8:e4m3", "guard": "stability>=0.92" },
    "gpt2::blocks.*/ff_matmul/*": { "precision": "int4", "max_cost_penalty": "1.15" }
  },
  "hints": ["low_latency"],
  "rounding_mode": "nearest",
  "quant_seed": "2026-03-20-01",
  "rollout": { "canary_dataset": "qa-small-v2", "canary_window_mins": "30" }
}
```

Mia: note: the profile JSON above has a nested rollout block — in control plane storage that's fine. eval-harness will emit: csv of per-op deltas, token_confidence histograms, and a small samples.jsonl of worst prompts. I'll wire a regression gate that fails the canary if any safety test flags.

Devon: about cost control — add a per-profile "cost_budget" knob (ops can specify a multiplier e.g. max_cost_penalty) so runtime can opt to limit the number of FP8 hot-swaps if infra cost budget exceeded.

Ashley: good idea. add cost_budget and graceful-eviction rules: if running above budget, evict lowest-impact FP8 overrides first (based on live importance metrics).

Leo: kernel registry API sketch: register_kernel(op_kind, precision, variant_id, binary_id, compatible_signature). runtime queries by op-id + precision and gets binary handle. keep API stable across minor schema versions.

InfraBot: images will include manifest of pre-baked binaries. we can lazily load 4-bit variants but require at least one higher-precision variant present to avoid total failure.

Mia: for telemetry, I'll propose the following metrics be emitted per-op: stability_score, token_confidence_mean, token_confidence_std, perp_delta_windowed, hot_swap_count, rollback_count. attach these to per-request traces.

SRE-Bot: also add a canary_timeline event stream so we can correlate alerts to the exact canary cohort.

Ashley: rollout playbook outline (short): 1) generate layered profile + eval diffs, 2) feature-flag canary on small cohort, 3) run CI-canary workloads + eval-harness, 4) monitor telemetry & alerts for 30m, 5) if pass -> widen, else rollback to base and create incident.

Devon: minor nit: decide whether guard expressions run in control plane or runtime. my vote: control plane evaluates simple guards (stability thresholds) for rollout decisions; runtime uses compiled threshold checks to avoid expensive parsing on hot path.

Leo: assign owners: Ashley -> playbook + rollout docs, Devon -> kernel registry + runtime pointer-swap, Mia -> eval harness + metrics, Infra -> image manifests + flags, SRE -> canary alerting config.

Ashley: thanks — will draft RFC follow-up with the playbook, API sketches, and a short migration guide for older profiles.

Mia: will prototype the harness changes and attach a sample CSV to the follow-up.

Devon: I'll spike the kernel registry later today and ping InfraBot for build slots.

Ashley: leaving this thread as canonical follow-up. next sync if needed Friday 9am.
